newsitem.title: FRANCE: ONIC says Argentina a threat to EU wheat exports.
newsitem.headline: ONIC says Argentina a threat to EU wheat exports.

text.p: The head of France's grain office ONIC said on Wednesday that cheaper Argentine wheat may significantly weigh on the pace of European Union and French wheat exports between December and March.
ONIC's director general said Argentine wheat was already depressing world markets but that competition may get worse when the bulk of the Argentine crop becomes available in December.
Alain Moulinier explained that unless the EU was ready to grant substantial export rebates to foil Argentine competition, the pace of EU wheat exports may decline during the period.
"Sustantial refunds would be needed. It is likely export levels will drop during that period," Moulinier told Reuters following a monthly news conference.
This would leave the EU with the last three months of the 1996/97 season to make up for ground lost earlier, he said.

Moulinier estimated that unless the EU managed to maintain its current wheat export pace of 300,000 tonnes per week, France would not meet the export target of six million tonnes of wheat it has set for 1996/97.
This would in turn result in sales to intervention stores.
"The French position is to maintain regular (wheat) exports to meet the six million tonnes target," he said.
"It is obvious that if we do not reach six million tonnes, wheat will be sold into intervention," he added
Moulinier said French wheat export commitments currently stood at 2.3 million tonnes.
The United States has repeatedly threatened to restore EEP export subsidies if the level of EU wheat export rebates threatened to undermine U.S. wheat prices.
But Moulinier said the debate was now "outdated," arguing it was Argentina and not the European Union that was depressing world prices.
He said that the European Commission was only keeping pace with lower world prices.
